chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Khalid ibn Yazeed Al-Qummy, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And they thought that there would be no affliction.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This was when the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was present among them, so they became blind and deaf. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, then Allah turned mercifully to them when Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) rose. He said: 'Then they became blind and deaf again until the Hour.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'And they thought that there would be no affliction' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the verse 'And they thought that there would be no affliction' (5:71) as a historical narrative of spiritual decline, noting that the Companions were blind and deaf to the truth during the Prophet's lifetime. After the Prophet's death, Allah granted them a period of mercy when Imam Ali (peace be upon him) rose to claim his right, but they subsequently returned to their state of spiritual blindness until the Day of Judgment. This interpretation highlights the pivotal role of Imam Ali in restoring divine guidance and serves as a critique of the broader community's failure to recognize his authority.
